amendments.body: Track `crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs` in version control. The whole new regression suite currently exists only as an untracked file (`crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:1`), so none of these alkalinity tests will ship or run in CI when this change is committed.
amendments.rationale: This is the only place the new alkalinity acceptance coverage lives. Leaving it untracked turns the code change into production behavior without the promised regression protection.

amendments.body: Unify the nitrification alkalinity default across construction paths. `ProcessParams::default()` now uses `NITRIFICATION_ALK_MEQ_PER_MG_N` at `crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:338`, but preset-backed states still come from a separate hard-coded literal in `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1018-1019`. Wire the preset default through the same constant (or add a regression asserting equality) so default-built tanks and preset/scenario tanks do not continue to simulate slightly different alkalinity depletion.
amendments.rationale: The point of introducing the named stoichiometric constant is to create a single source of truth. Leaving the preset literal stale preserves two behaviors for the same parameter and can cause drift between unit-test fixtures and scenario seeds.

amendments.body: Fix the alkalinity assertion diagnostics in `crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:472-475` and `crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:495-503`. The new `Element::Alkalinity` path compares meq values, but the per-system and per-tick panic text still labels those values as `mg`, so a failing alkalinity check will report the wrong unit.
amendments.rationale: These helpers are used to diagnose scientific-budget regressions. Reporting alkalinity in the wrong unit is a correctness problem for debugging and calibration, not just wording.

payload.summary: Reviewed the diff plus the nested worktree changes end-to-end. I found three actionable issues: the new alkalinity regression file is still untracked, the new stoichiometric constant is not yet the single source of truth because presets still hard-code `0.1428`, and the new alkalinity budget-helper diagnostics still print `mg` instead of `meq`. I also ran `cargo test -p tank_core --test nitrification_alkalinity --test plant_nutrient_normalization` and `cargo test -p tank_core`; the targeted tests passed, and the full suite still shows the existing `save_load_with_active_cycle_state` failure that is already present at the checked-in `HEAD` of the nested worktree.
